annotatedSteps.description: Assume 5 − 2√3 is rational and express √3 in terms of integers a and b
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
Let 5 − 2√3 be rational. Then 5 − 2√3 = a/b, where a and b are integers and b ≠ 0.
⇒ 2√3 = 5 − a/b = (5b − a)/b
⇒ √3 = (5b − a)/(2b)
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct assumption and algebraic rearrangement to isolate √3

annotatedSteps.description: Deduce contradiction and state final conclusion that 5 − 2√3 is irrational
annotatedSteps.studentWork: Since a and b are integers, (5b − a)/(2b) is rational, but √3 is irrational. This is a contradiction.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ½ Contradiction noted, but explicit final conclusion ('Therefore, 5 − 2√3 is irrational') is missing
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: Since a and b are integers, (5b − a)/(2b) is rational, but √3 is irrational. This contradicts the given fact that √3 is irrational. Hence, our assumption is incorrect, and 5 − 2√3 is an irrational number.

teacherNote: Your algebraic rearrangement and identification of the contradiction are spot on. Remember to always write the concluding statement ('Therefore, 5 − 2√3 is irrational') to secure full marks in proof questions.
